concepts.def: Base-2 number system using only digits 0 and 1, the native language of digital computers.

concepts.def: Base-16 number system using digits 0-9 and letters A-F, compactly representing binary.
A single hexadecimal symbol representing 4 bits (a nibble), values 0-15.
A group of 4 bits, exactly representable by one hexadecimal digit.
Group binary digits into nibbles from the right, then convert each group to a hex digit.

concepts.def: Programming language close to human language (Python, Java) that must be translated to machine code.

concepts.def: Whole number with no fractional part, positive, negative or zero (e.g., 7, -42, 0).

concepts.def: Named storage location whose value can change during program execution.

Name given to a variable, constant, function or other element, following naming rules.
